A Lean-checked obstruction to four-color triangle set palettes on K5

DRAFT - research manuscript, 1 November 2026. No human authorship or affiliation is asserted. Prepared with AI assistance. Zero accepted campaign credit; root adjudication, final replay and paper review remain pending.

Every assignment of four available color labels to the ten edges of the complete graph K5 gives two distinct triangles with the same set of edge colors. We present a finite exhaustion proof and a Lean certificate connecting that computation to arbitrary undirected edge colorings. The obstruction refutes Conjecture 5 of Pilsniak and Wozniak [1, p. 4], which asserts that the minimum number of labels for triangle set distinction is n - 1 for every n >= 4. Repetitions and unused labels are allowed throughout. The argument does not determine the exact minimum at five and does not refute the separate multiset conjecture.
1. The source assertion and the result

Let V = {0,...,n-1}, let E be its two-element subsets, and let T be its three-element subsets. For a map c: E -> {0,...,k-1}, define P_c(t) = {c(e): e is a two-element subset of t}. These are sets: a color occurring twice contributes only one element. Call c distinguishing if P_c is injective on T. No properness or surjectivity condition is imposed.

Write A(n,k) for the existence of such a distinguishing coloring. The source invariant tau_s(n) is the least k for which A(n,k) holds. This minimum exists at the orders considered: giving each edge a different color distinguishes triangles, since their sets of edge labels determine their edge sets. Relabeling the source labels 1,...,k by 0,...,k-1 changes no palette equality.
Theorem. Four labels do not suffice at order five.
For every c: E(K5) -> {0,1,2,3}, there exist distinct t,u in T(K5) with P_c(t) = P_c(u). Equivalently, A(5,4) is false.

Corollary. The assertion "for every n >= 4, tau_s(n) = n - 1" in [1, Conjecture 5] is false. Indeed its instance n = 5 would supply A(5,4), contrary to the theorem. A coloring using fewer labels embeds into four labels, so allowing unused labels introduces no loophole. No exact value of tau_s(5) is claimed here.
2. A finite problem with full coverage

Order the undirected edges as 01,02,03,04,12,13,14,23,24,34 and denote their colors by a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h,i,j. Increasing pairs represent each undirected edge exactly once. Similarly increasing triples represent exactly the ten triangles. Their palettes are as follows; braces erase repetitions.

Thus arbitrary colorings are in bijection with all 4^10 = 1,048,576 words of length ten over four labels. There is no quotient by symmetry, no exclusion of adjacent equal colors, and no requirement to use all labels. The incidence table follows by taking the three two-subsets of each triple. A word distinguishes precisely when the ten displayed sets are pairwise different.

The independent source reviewer used this unpruned algorithm with actual sets and independently generated incidence. It visited every full word and found no witness; the maximum observed number of distinct palettes was nine. The technical reviewer separately regenerated incidence and repeated an unpruned scan. Their preserved programs and full summary outputs are corroboration, not numeric premises imported into Lean.

Coverage is elementary: each of the ten coordinates is independently free to be any of four values, so the Cartesian product lists every map exactly once. The predicate in the loop is equivalent to palette injectivity by the table. Consequently a correct execution returning NO_WITNESS proves the theorem. The kernel certificate below verifies a more efficient collision-pruned form of this same finite obstruction; no million-line case printout is needed.

A simple count of available sets cannot establish the result. Four labels allow 4 singleton, 6 two-element and 4 three-element palettes, totaling 14 > 10. The obstruction concerns compatibility of palettes on shared edges, rather than an insufficiency of abstract palette names.
3. Collision pruning and a checked finite lemma

For labels x,y,z in {0,1,2,3}, put B(x,y,z) = 2^x OR 2^y OR 2^z, where OR is bitwise inclusive disjunction. The bit in position q is present exactly when q belongs to {x,y,z}. Repetitions have no effect. In particular equality of codes implies equality of palettes. The formal lemma code_sound verifies this implication on the finite label type; its proof is by kernel decide, with no external computation premise.

The checker processes a,...,j in edge order. A triangle is complete once its three coordinates are assigned. Each unordered pair of triangles is tested at the first depth where both are complete. If a collision is found, every extension of that prefix already fails injectivity, so the checker returns true on that branch. Otherwise it conjoins the results of all four assignments to the next coordinate. A complete word with no collision returns false.

No pair can cease to collide: subsequent assignments affect neither completed triangle. Conversely, a hypothetical collision-free word can be followed through every conjunction, and none of its collision branches is taken. It would reach false. This is the direction of soundness required to rule out witnesses.

Depths zero through five only branch. The 45 tests at depths six through ten are exactly the 45 unordered pairs of ten triangles, each once. For example depth six compares {a,b,e} with {a,c,f}; depth seven adds comparisons of {a,d,g} with each of these. The remaining tests are obtained mechanically from the incidence table and the maximum coordinate index in each pair. The reviewer checked this complete pair coverage separately.

The literal checker has definitions check10 through check0 and all4(f) = f(0) AND f(1) AND f(2) AND f(3). Its theorem check_pass states check0 = true and is proved by decide. all4_spec identifies this Boolean conjunction with universal truth over Fin 4. In code_no, assuming all 45 code inequalities, successive applications of all4_spec follow an arbitrary word; the inequalities remove every conditional collision exit and yield false = true. Thus the finite calculation and its mathematical use are both kernel checked.
4. Formal correspondence to the graph assertion

The four immutable mathematical modules are Defs.lean, BoolProbe.lean, Checker.lean and Endpoint.lean. The last defines Edge n as the subtype of Fin n x Fin n with first coordinate less than second, and Triangle n as increasing triples. trianglePalette c t is the Finset of colors on its three actual edges. The long edge inequality follows by transitivity. No directed duplicate, loop or phantom triangle is introduced.
Set triple; OR code; code equality implies set equality
Every four-label K5 coloring fails injectivity
Negation of the named universal assertion

The theorem no_four starts from a hypothetical injective palette map. Each two different concrete increasing triples t0,...,t9 must have different palettes. If their codes were equal, code_sound would give equal palettes and injectivity would identify the triples, contradicting their explicit inequality. These 45 code inequalities contradict code_no. This bridge rules out actual arbitrary graph colorings, not merely an independently defined Boolean surrogate.

Achievable n k :=
  exists c : Edge n -> Fin k,
    Function.Injective (trianglePalette c)
SourceClaim := forall n, 4 <= n ->
  IsLeast {k : Nat | Achievable n k} (n - 1)
source_refutation : not SourceClaim

IsLeast S m means both m belongs to S and m <= k for every k in S. Membership at n = 5 alone supplies a four-label coloring; no minimization algorithm or unproved numerical bound is required. The Lean endpoint obtains this membership, extracts c and its injectivity, and applies no_four. Natural subtraction agrees with ordinary subtraction in the stated range.

The definitions preserve the source distinction between arbitrary colorings and proper colorings, and between sets and multisets. For instance pal 0 0 1 equals pal 0 1 1. Separate reviewer sanity examples kernel-check this equality, cardinalities ten for both Edge 5 and Triangle 5, and the constant coloring palette {0}. The helpers and the formalization receive no separate mathematical credit.

The primary source [1] is the five-page arXiv:2407.19050v1 dated 26 July 2024. Its page 2 distinguishes the proper invariant tau-prime, the unrestricted multiset invariant tau_m and the unrestricted set invariant tau_s. Conjecture 5 on page 4 quantifies every n >= 4. Figure 1 on page 5 supplies examples at orders four and six, placing five strictly between the supporting examples. The obstruction is a refutation of a named universal mathematical assertion at an admissible interior order.

Theorem 1 of [1] determines the proper-coloring minimum as n for odd n and n+1 for even n. Its rainbow-palette lower bound requires properness, which is absent here. It cannot exclude all arbitrary four-label colorings of K5. Theorem 3 proves tau_m(n) >= n-1 for n >= 4. At five this gives only a lower bound of four, and the displayed inequality tau_m <= tau_s <= tau-prime supplies no strictness at four. Neither theorem yields the present obstruction. Conjecture 4 for multisets is unaffected: unequal multiplicities can distinguish triangles whose sets coincide.

The independent source review also read selected relevant primary bodies of nearby work. Theorem 6 of [2] concerns color-blind vertex palettes: sorted incident multiplicities with color names forgotten. Its K5 concerns five vertex objects, not ten named triangle sets. The total-coloring work [3] uses vertex/edge contributions to sums at adjacent vertices. Theorem 4.3 of [4], with Lemmas 4.1 and 4.2, provides quasi-majority neighbor sum distinction. Its additive vertex data do not imply an impossibility theorem for injective triangle sets. These are substantive object distinctions, not a claim that titles alone exclude subsumption.
